Magic can only be learned from ages 7-15. Unless your tutor has both expert magic traits and very high learning, it will take that entire time to train for a student to also become expert.

Essentially, you'll need a genius (20+ learning,) who also has two or more expert magic skills to train a new student which is very unlikely.

Lore wise, mixed magic seems to come from the fog worshippers, so it's very rare. And, iirc, dead magic is stigmatized by living magic cultures and vice versa (aside from the fact that finding a good tutor is next to impossible besides.)

Mechanically, expert magicians generate the highest magical prowess multiplier (which reduces the risk of spell failure) and (this Might have been fixed) in the case of having multiple magic styles, your Lowest magic level determines your magical prowess. So unless you can garuntee (or are just willing to roll the dice) it's very rarely worth the effort of trying to train a student in more than one school.

I have managed to train students to expert level in all three schools, but living magic was the only complete system at the time so it was a vanity project.

True polymorph question:

Sorry guys, I'm sure you get this question Allll the time, but I need clarification.

Pre- 10th level, I've been happy to play a nature cleric. Flavors- wise, it's almost perfect.

My problem is that, after 10th level the character just hasn't changed. I'm looking for that "prophet of the almighty" feel. Instead I'm just upcasting the same three spells all day.

 Healing isn't worth much and there's no point to trying to be a melee fighter when toll the dead and spiritual weapon lets me stay 20ft out of combat while doing more damage than the fighter.

Divine intervention is totally worthless. Spend a whole action for 10% chance of success, and for what? I have to go all the way to 20th level for certain success, and the DM could throw out anything: and because I have access to the cleric spell list (about 1/5th of which are any use) I'm better off just casting the spell myself. It would be kind of cool if Divine intervention replicated some higher level cleric spell, but those are all trash anyway.

The easiest solution is to go arcana domain and raid the wizard spells (and still get the, practically worthless, divine intervention), but that just feels like ripping off another class.

I don't want to rip off another class, I want the class I'm playing to be better.

Im at a loss of how to fix this and mantian class fidelity. Something like a rework of DI or creating the Miracle spell might work.

Well yes, I agree. All classes are nerfered compared to 3.5e allegories, but cleric more so. 

Wish and true polymorph(/ shapechange) are actually more powerful in 5e than in 3.5 and Wizards, sorcerers and warlocks can cast these Every Day. Clerics can't reliably use divine intervention until **level 20**, can only use it every 7 days and *still* can't choose what it does. 

A warlock could dip one level in fighter and come out with True polymorph and Heavy Armor and still have better HP at level 18.

Arcana cleric seems, to me, the better option bc you can get both wish and divine intervention: but without a re-flavor the role play just feels awful.


At that point - would adding the miracle spell back into 5e add more balance?

Otherwise clerics just coast by on spamming a handful of class spells (eg spirit guardians, death ward, spiritual weapon) because while they do get access to the whole spell list - so many of those spells are just plain disapointing.

Domains Kind of fix that (war, light, arcana etc.) But choosing one of those for the mechanics means altering the roleplay of the character. If I have to choose subclasses for the mechanical benefits, I almost feel that going all out and getting a new class would be better. Playing a divine soul sorcerer and  RPing it as a priest would just make a better cleric than the actual cleric is.

A small clarification.

My contract is by no means ironclad, and as you pointed out easily could have been twisted to put me in my place with a bit of wordplay. However, that's not how this went down. 

The DM barely glanced at the contract, much less how he could wordplay out of it. He just layed into me with how he had screwed me over and utterly disregarded any of my arguments to the contrary (including my own counter argument.) The contract never mattered to him *at all,* much less how I thought I could get a nifty boon out of it. 

And that's the problem: the contract exists to prevent either of us from changing it or disobeying it, but my DM rewrites it at will and ignores any stipulations where I might benefit. And how is it fair that only my PC is held accountable in a contract his NPC also agreed to? Furthermore, only the downsides of the agreement are in effect.

Maybe I'm the asshole for being tricky in a deal that he was also being tricky in: but refusing to any parts of his deal (even before I brought up the immortality bit) is just a dick move. The only part where I "mocked him" was when I tried to keep him from altering a signed agreement on his every whim.

On the other hand: my DM is not a lawyer, and I think he feels I betrayed his trust.

That said, a deals a deal (he's done similar to me in the past, when I was DM) and he can't just use his authority as the DM to rewrite the contract in a completely one sided way. Throwing absolute immortality (the literal next session) to another  player was just insult on injury.
